title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第三十四 良政
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第三十四 良政 Volume 53 Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五十三‧列傳第三十四 良政

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53, Biographies 34: Good Governance
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 53, Biographies 34: Virtuous Officials

sentences.zh: 傅琰 虞愿 劉懷慰 裴昭明 沈憲 李珪之 孔琇之

translations.literal: Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Liu Huaiwei, Pei Zhaoming, Shen Xian, Li Guizhi, Kong Xiuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yan, Yu Yuan, Liu Huaiwei, Pei Zhaoming, Shen Xian, Li Guizhi, and Kong Xiuzhi

sentences.zh: 太祖承宋氏奢縱，風移百城，輔立幼主，思振民瘼。

translations.literal: The Founder inherited the Song clan's luxury and laxity; custom shifted through a hundred cities. He assisted in establishing a young lord and thought to revive the people's afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor inherited the Song dynasty's extravagance and lax rule, which had spread decadent habits through cities everywhere. Supporting a young sovereign on the throne, he sought to relieve the people's distress.

sentences.zh: 爲政未朞，擢山陰令傅琰爲益州刺史。

translations.literal: His governance had not yet reached its term when he promoted Fu Yan, magistrate of Shanyin, to Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign he promoted Fu Yan, the magistrate of Shanyin, to regional inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 乃捐華反樸，恭己南面，導民以躬，意存勿擾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cast aside splendor and returned to simplicity, held himself reverently facing south, guided the people by his own person, and his intent was to leave them undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He renounced ornament for plain living, held himself with humble dignity on the throne, led the people by personal example, and kept administration as unobtrusive as possible.

sentences.zh: 以山陰大邑，獄訟繁滋，建元三年，別置獄丞，與建康爲比。

translations.literal: Because Shanyin was a great district and prison lawsuits proliferated, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison assistant was appointed, on a par with Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shanyin was a large district with a heavy caseload, in the third year of Jianyuan a separate prison deputy was appointed, matching the arrangement at the capital.

sentences.zh: 永明繼運，垂心治術。

translations.literal: When Yongming succeeded to the mandate, he bent his mind to the art of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yongming reign the court devoted itself earnestly to the art of government.

sentences.zh: 杖威善斷，猶多漏網，長吏犯法，封刃行誅。

translations.literal: Relying on authority and skilled in judgment, yet many still escaped the net; when senior officials violated the law, the blade was sealed and execution carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The court wielded stern authority and judged cases decisively, yet many offenders still slipped through; when senior officials broke the law, swords were drawn and punishment was enforced without delay.

sentences.zh: 郡縣居職，以三周爲小滿。

translations.literal: For those serving in commanderies and districts, three cycles were taken as a minor fulfillment of term.
translations.idiomatic: Officials serving in the commanderies and districts were expected to complete three annual cycles before their term was considered minimally fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 水旱之災，輙加賑卹。

translations.literal: When flood or drought disasters occurred, relief and succor were always added.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever floods or droughts struck, the government promptly provided relief.

sentences.zh: 明帝自在布衣，曉達吏事，君臨億兆，專務刀筆，未嘗枉法申恩，守宰以之肅震。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, from the time he was in common cloth, understood administrative affairs. When he ruled over the hundred millions, he devoted himself solely to legal documents and the brush; he never bent the law to show favor, and prefects and magistrates were thereby awed into reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had understood official business since his days as a commoner. Once he ruled the realm, he devoted himself entirely to legal paperwork, never bending the law to show favor, and prefects and magistrates were awed into strict compliance.

sentences.zh: 永明之世，十許年中，百姓無雞鳴犬吠之警，都邑之盛，士女富逸，歌聲舞節，袨服華粧，桃花綠水之間，秋月春風之下，蓋以百數。

translations.literal: In the age of Yongming, for some ten years the common people had no alarm of cockcrow or dog bark. The splendor of the capital: gentlemen and ladies rich and at ease, songs and dance to the measure, splendid dress and gorgeous adornment—between peach blossom and green water, under autumn moon and spring breeze—were reckoned in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongming era, for roughly ten years the people knew no disturbance even of cockcrow or barking dogs. The capital flourished: men and women lived in comfort and affluence, with song and dance everywhere, fine dress and splendid adornment—amid peach blossoms and green waters, under autumn moons and spring breezes—numbering in the hundreds of such scenes.

sentences.zh: 及建武之興，虜難猋急，征役連歲，不遑啓居，軍國糜耗，從此衰矣。

translations.literal: When Jianwu arose, barbarian troubles blew fierce; levies and corvée continued year after year, with no leisure to open one's door and dwell in peace. Army and state were worn down and exhausted—from this the decline began.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jianwu era began, northern raids grew fierce; conscription and corvée continued year after year, leaving people no peace at home. Army and state were drained dry, and from that point the dynasty declined.

sentences.zh: 齊世善政著名表績無幾焉，位次遷升，非直止乎城邑。

translations.literal: In the Qi age, those of good governance with famous recorded achievements were few; rank and advancement in office did not stop merely at cities and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi dynasty, officials famed for good governance and recorded achievements were few, and promotion in rank was not limited to service within cities and districts alone.

sentences.zh: 今取其清察有迹者，餘則隨以附焉。

translations.literal: Now we take those whose clarity and scrutiny left traces; the rest are attached accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Here we include those whose integrity and sharp administration left a clear record; the remainder are noted in passing where relevant.

sentences.zh: 傅琰字季珪，北地靈州人也。

translations.literal: Fu Yan, style name Jigui, was a man of Lingzhou in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yan, courtesy name Jigui, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖邵，員外郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was a Staff Gentleman Outside the Office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao served as an outside-office gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父僧祐，安東錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Sengyou was Recorder-Adjutant of Andong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengyou served as recorder-adjutant under the Andong commandery.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，遷山陰令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi he was transferred to magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi he was appointed magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 山陰，東土大縣，難爲長官，僧祐在縣有稱，琰尤明察，又著能名。

translations.literal: Shanyin was a great district of the eastern lands, difficult to govern as chief official. Sengyou had a reputation in the district; Yan was especially perspicacious and also gained a name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyin was a major district in the eastern region and a difficult post for any magistrate. Sengyou had earned a reputation there, and Yan was especially sharp-eyed in judgment, winning renown for his competence as well.

sentences.zh: 其年爵新亭侯。

translations.literal: That year he was ennobled as Marquis of Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was ennobled as Marquis of Xinting.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was transferred to Right Assistant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhui reign he was promoted to right assistant director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，居南岸，隣家失火，延燒琰屋，琰抱柩不動，隣人競來赴救，乃得俱全。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was in mourning, dwelling on the south bank. A neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to burn Yan's house. Yan embraced the coffin and did not move; neighbors rushed in competition to rescue, and thus all was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning he lived on the south bank. A neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to Yan's dwelling. He clung to the coffin and would not move; neighbors rushed to help, and mother and coffin were saved unharmed.

sentences.zh: 琰股髀之閒，已被煙焰。

translations.literal: Between Yan's thighs and buttocks he had already been touched by smoke and flame.
translations.idiomatic: The flesh between his thighs had already been scorched by smoke and flame.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除邵陵王左軍諮議，江夏王錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Consultant of the Left Army under the Prince of Shaoling and Recorder-Adjutant under the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed consultant to the left army of the Prince of Shaoling and recorder-adjutant to the Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，以山陰獄訟煩積，復以琰爲山陰令。

translations.literal: When the Founder assisted in government, because prison lawsuits in Shanyin piled up in annoyance, he again appointed Yan magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor served as regent, lawsuits in Shanyin had again piled up, so he reappointed Yan as magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 賣針賣糖老姥爭團絲，來詣琰，琰不辨覈，縳團絲於柱鞭之，密視有鐵屑，乃罰賣糖者。

translations.literal: An old woman who sold needles and an old woman who sold sugar disputed a ball of silk thread and came before Yan. Yan did not distinguish and verify; he bound the silk ball to a pillar and flogged it, secretly watched and saw iron filings, and then punished the sugar-seller.
translations.idiomatic: An old woman who sold needles and one who sold sugar disputed a ball of silk and brought the case to Yan. Without questioning either party, he tied the silk to a pillar and whipped it; watching closely, he saw iron filings and then punished the sugar-seller.

sentences.zh: 二野父爭雞，琰各問「何以食雞」，一人云「粟」，一人云「豆」，乃破雞得粟，罪言豆者。

translations.literal: Two countrymen disputed a chicken. Yan asked each, 'With what do you feed the chicken?' One said 'millet,' one said 'beans.' He then broke open the chicken and found millet, and punished the one who had said beans.
translations.idiomatic: Two peasants disputed ownership of a chicken. Yan asked each what he fed it; one said millet, the other beans. He slaughtered the bird, found millet in its crop, and punished the man who had claimed beans.

sentences.zh: 縣內稱神明，無敢復爲偷盜。

translations.literal: Within the district he was called divine and perspicacious; none dared again to be thieves.
translations.idiomatic: The district hailed him as uncannily wise, and no one dared steal again.

sentences.zh: 琰父子竝著奇績，江左鮮有。

translations.literal: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary records; east of the Yangtze there were few such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son Yan together achieved extraordinary records, rarely matched in the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 世云「諸傅有《治縣譜》，子孫相傳，不以示人」。

translations.literal: The age says, 'The various Fu have a Register of Governing Districts, handed down among descendants and not shown to others.'
translations.idiomatic: People said that the Fu clan possessed a manual on governing districts, passed down among descendants and never shown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 臨淮劉玄明亦有吏能，爲山陰令，大著名績。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanming of Linhuai also had administrative ability; as magistrate of Shanyin he achieved great recorded achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanming of Linhuai was also a capable administrator; as magistrate of Shanyin he won great renown.

sentences.zh: 琰子翽問之，玄明曰：「我臨去當告卿。

translations.literal: Yan's son Ao asked him. Xuanming said, 'When I am about to leave I shall tell you.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Ao asked him for advice. Xuanming said, 'When I am about to leave office I will tell you.'

sentences.zh: 」將別，謂之曰：「作縣唯日食一升飰，而莫飲酒。」

translations.literal: ' As they were about to part, he said to him, 'Governing a district—only eat one sheng of rice per day, and do not drink wine.'
translations.idiomatic: As they parted, he told him, 'As magistrate, eat only one sheng of rice a day and never touch wine.'

sentences.zh: 虞愿字士恭，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yuan, style name Shigong, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan, courtesy name Shigong, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖賚，給事中，監利侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ben was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Marquis of Jianli.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ben served as attendant within the yellow gates and was ennobled as Marquis of Jianli.

sentences.zh: 父望之，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Wangzhi died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wangzhi died young.

sentences.zh: 賚中庭橘樹冬熟，子孫競來取之，愿年數歲，獨不取，賚及家人皆異之。

translations.literal: In Ben's courtyard an orange tree ripened in winter; descendants competed to come and take them. Yuan was several years old and alone did not take any; Ben and the family all regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: An orange tree in Ben's courtyard ripened in winter, and the grandchildren rushed to pick the fruit. Yuan was only a few years old and alone refused to take any; Ben and the whole family marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，爲國子生，再遷湘東王國常侍，轉潯陽王府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia he was a student of the Imperial Academy; after two promotions he became Regular Attendant of the Kingdom of Xiangdong, then transferred to Ink-Office Adjutant of the mansion of the Prince of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanjia era he entered the Imperial Academy; he was twice promoted to regular attendant of the Prince of Xiangdong's household, then transferred to ink-office adjutant under the Prince of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，以愿儒吏學涉，兼蕃國舊恩，意遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, because Yuan was a Confucian official of broad learning, and also because of old favor from the feudal state, his intent and treatment were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he favored Yuan greatly for his learning and skill as a scholar-official and for their old bond from the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 除太常丞，尚書祠部郎，通直散騎侍郎，領五郡中正，祠部郎如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Master of Writing in the Department of Sacrifices, Palace Attendant of Regular Emergent Cavalry, and concurrently Director of Rectitude for five commanderies, with the post of Master of Sacrifices as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, director in the sacrifices office of the Masters of Writing, palace attendant in the emergent cavalry, and concurrently director of rectitude for five commanderies, while retaining his sacrifices post.

sentences.zh: 帝性猜忌，體肥憎風，夏月常著皮小衣，拜左右二人爲司風令史，風起方面，輙先啓聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor's nature was suspicious; his body was stout and he hated wind. In summer months he often wore small leather garments. He appointed two attendants at his side as Wind-Order Clerks; when wind rose from any quarter they always reported first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was suspicious by nature, corpulent, and hated drafts. In summer he often wore a small leather vest. He appointed two attendants as wind-watch clerks who always reported the moment a breeze rose from any direction.

sentences.zh: 星文災變，不信太史，不聽外奏，勑靈臺知星二人給愿，常直內省，有異先啓，以相檢察。

translations.literal: For stellar signs and calamitous changes he did not trust the Grand Astrologer and would not listen to outside memorials. He ordered two star-knowers of the Spirit Terrace assigned to Yuan, who constantly attended inside the palace; if there was anything unusual they reported first, for mutual inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He did not trust the grand astrologer on celestial omens and refused outside reports. He assigned two observatory astronomers to Yuan, who kept constant watch inside the palace and reported any anomaly at once so the reports could be cross-checked.

sentences.zh: 帝以故宅起湘宮寺，費極奢侈。

translations.literal: The Emperor raised the Xiang Palace Temple on his former residence; the expense was extremely luxurious.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor built the Xiang Palace Temple on the site of his former residence at enormous expense.

sentences.zh: 以孝武莊嚴剎七層，帝欲起十層，不可立，分爲兩剎，各五層。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had seven stories, the Emperor wished to build ten; it could not stand, so it was divided into two monasteries of five stories each.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's Zhuangyan Monastery had stood seven stories high; the emperor wanted ten but the structure would not bear it, so he split it into two pagodas of five stories each.

sentences.zh: 新安太守巢尚之罷郡還，見帝，曰：「卿至湘宮寺未？

translations.literal: Chao Shangzhi, Grand Administrator of Xin'an, finished his commandery and returned; seeing the Emperor he said, 'Have you been to the Xiang Palace Temple yet?'
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shangzhi, who had finished his term as grand administrator of Xin'an, came to court and asked the emperor, 'Have you visited the Xiang Palace Temple yet?'

sentences.zh: 我起此寺，是大功德。

translations.literal: I raised this temple—it is great merit.
translations.idiomatic: I built this temple—it is a great act of merit.

sentences.zh: 」愿在側曰：「陛下起此寺，皆是百姓賣兒貼婦錢，佛若有知，當悲哭哀愍，罪高佛圖，有何功德？

translations.literal: ' Yuan at his side said, 'Your Majesty raised this temple—all of it is money from the common people selling sons and pawning wives. If Buddha had knowledge, he would weep in grief and pity; the guilt exceeds Buddha's stupa—what merit is there?'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, standing beside them, said, 'Your Majesty, this temple was paid for with money from common folk who sold their sons and pawned their wives. If the Buddha knew, he would weep in pity; the sin towers higher than any pagoda—where is the merit in that?'

sentences.zh: 」尚書令袁粲在坐，爲之失色。

translations.literal: ' Minister-in-Chief Yuan Can was seated and lost color on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Minister-in-Chief Yuan Can, who was present, turned pale at this.

sentences.zh: 帝乃怒，使人驅下殿，愿徐去無異容。

translations.literal: The Emperor then grew angry and had men drive him down from the hall. Yuan departed slowly without change of countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had him driven from the hall. Yuan withdrew slowly, his expression unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以舊恩，少日中，已復召入。

translations.literal: Because of old favor, before midday he was again summoned in.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to their old bond, he was summoned back before noon the same day.

sentences.zh: 帝好圍碁，甚拙，去格七八道，物議共欺爲第三品。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved weiqi and was very clumsy, placing stones seven or eight lines from the grid; public opinion together deceived him into thinking he was third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved go but played very poorly, often placing stones seven or eight lines off the grid; court opinion collectively humored him into believing he ranked third class.

sentences.zh: 與第一品王抗圍碁，依品賭戲，抗每饒借之，曰：「皇帝飛碁，臣抗不能斷。

translations.literal: Playing weiqi with first-rank Wang Kang, they wagered according to rank. Kang always yielded to him, saying, 'The Emperor's flying stones—your subject Kang cannot cut them off.'
translations.idiomatic: When he played go with first-rank master Wang Kang, they wagered by rank. Kang always let him win, saying, 'Your Majesty's stones fly so fast that I, Kang, cannot block them.'

sentences.zh: 」帝終不覺，以爲信然，好之愈篤。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor to the end did not perceive it, believed it true, and loved it all the more ardently.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor never caught on, took it all at face value, and grew fonder of the game than ever.

sentences.zh: 愿又曰：「堯以此教丹朱，非人主所宜好也。

translations.literal: Yuan again said, 'Yao used this to teach Danzhu—it is not what a lord of men ought to love.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan added, 'Yao used this game to teach his son Danzhu—it is not a pastime fit for a sovereign.'

sentences.zh: 」雖數忤旨，而蒙賞賜，猶異餘人。

translations.literal: ' Though he repeatedly went against the imperial intent, he received rewards and gifts still different from others.
translations.idiomatic: Though he often spoke against the emperor's wishes, he still received rewards unlike anyone else.

sentences.zh: 遷兼中書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent Master of Writing in the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to concurrent director in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝寢疾，愿常侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took to his bed with illness, Yuan constantly attended with medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell gravely ill, Yuan constantly attended him at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 帝素能食，尤好逐夷，以銀缽盛蜜漬之，一食數缽。

translations.literal: The Emperor had always been able to eat and especially loved zhuyi; he stored it in silver bowls steeped in honey and ate several bowls at one sitting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always been a hearty eater and especially loved cured fish called zhuyi, which he kept in silver bowls steeped in honey and consumed by the bowlful.

sentences.zh: 謂揚州刺史王景文曰：「此是奇味，卿頗足不？

translations.literal: He said to Wang Jingwen, Governor of Yangzhou, 'This is a marvelous flavor—do you have enough of it?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked Wang Jingwen, governor of Yangzhou, 'This is a rare delicacy—do you get enough of it?'

sentences.zh: 」景文曰：「臣夙好此物，貧素致之甚難。

translations.literal: ' Jingwen said, 'Your subject has long loved this thing; in poverty and plain living it is very hard to obtain.'
translations.idiomatic: Jingwen replied, 'I have always loved it, but in my humble circumstances it is very hard to come by.'

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅。

translations.literal: ' The Emperor was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 食逐夷積多，胷腹痞脹，氣將絕。

translations.literal: Eating zhuyi accumulated in quantity, his chest and belly became blocked and distended, and his breath was about to cease.
translations.idiomatic: After eating too much zhuyi, his chest and belly swelled with blockage until he was near death.

sentences.zh: 左右啓飲數升酢酒，乃消。

translations.literal: Those at his side reported that drinking several sheng of vinegar wine would then dissolve it.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants advised him to drink several sheng of vinegar wine, and the swelling subsided.

sentences.zh: 疾大困，一食汁滓猶至三升，水患積久，藥不復效。

translations.literal: His illness grew greatly distressed; in one meal the dregs of broth still reached three sheng. Water illness had accumulated long; medicine no longer had effect.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, he still consumed up to three sheng of broth dregs at a single meal. Edema had built up over time, and medicine no longer helped.

sentences.zh: 大漸日，正坐，呼道人，合掌便絕。

translations.literal: On the day of his great decline he sat upright, called for a Daoist priest, joined his palms, and then expired.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he neared death he sat upright, summoned a Daoist priest, pressed his palms together, and died.

sentences.zh: 愿以侍疾久，轉正員郎。

translations.literal: Because Yuan had long attended the illness, he was transferred to regular Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuan had long attended him in illness, he was promoted to regular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉平太守，在郡不治生產。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Jinping; in the commandery he did not manage production for profit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as grand administrator of Jinping and made no effort to enrich himself in office.

sentences.zh: 前政與民交關，質錄其兒婦，愿遣人於道奪取將還。

translations.literal: The previous administration had dealings with the people and took their sons and daughters-in-law as pledges in custody. Yuan sent men on the road to seize them back and return them.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor had seized commoners' sons and daughters-in-law as collateral for debts; Yuan sent men to intercept them on the road and bring them home.

sentences.zh: 在郡立學堂教授。

translations.literal: In the commandery he established a school hall for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he founded a school and taught there himself.

sentences.zh: 郡舊出髯蛇膽，可爲藥，有餉愿蛇者，愿不忍殺，放二十里外山中，一夜蛇還牀下。

translations.literal: The commandery traditionally produced bearded-snake gall, usable as medicine. Someone presented Yuan with a snake; Yuan could not bear to kill it and released it in the mountains twenty li away. In one night the snake returned beneath his bed.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was known for bearded-snake gall used in medicine. When someone presented Yuan with a snake, he could not bear to kill it and released it twenty li into the hills; overnight the snake returned to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 復送四十里外山，經宿，復還故處。

translations.literal: He again sent it forty li into the mountains; after one night it again returned to its former place.
translations.idiomatic: He released it again forty li into the mountains, but after a night it came back once more.

sentences.zh: 愿更令遠，乃不復歸，論者以爲仁心所致也。

translations.literal: Yuan again had it sent farther, and then it did not return; commentators thought this was caused by his benevolent heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had it taken still farther away, and then it did not return; commentators attributed this to the power of his compassionate heart.

sentences.zh: 海邊有越王石，常隱雲霧。

translations.literal: By the seashore there was a Yue-king stone, which often hid in cloud and mist.
translations.idiomatic: On the coast there was a stone called the Yue King's Stone, usually hidden in cloud and mist.

sentences.zh: 相傳云：「清廉太守乃得見。

translations.literal: Tradition says, 'Only an incorrupt grand administrator can see it.'
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that only an incorrupt grand administrator could see it.

sentences.zh: 」愿往觀視，清徹無隱蔽。

translations.literal: ' Yuan went to observe it; it was clear and limpid with nothing hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan went to look, and the stone stood clear before him with nothing concealed.

sentences.zh: 後琅邪王秀之爲郡，與朝士書曰：「此郡承虞公之後，善政猶存，遺風易遵，差得無事。

translations.literal: Later when Wang Xiuzhi of Langya governed the commandery, he wrote to court gentlemen, 'This commandery follows after Lord Yu; good governance still remains, the legacy wind is easy to follow—one can get by with little trouble.'
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wang Xiuzhi of Langya took the post, he wrote to colleagues at court, 'This commandery still bears the legacy of Lord Yu; good governance endures, his example is easy to follow, and affairs are largely untroubled.'

sentences.zh: 」以母老解職，除後軍將軍。

translations.literal: ' Because his mother was old he resigned his post and was appointed General of the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned because his mother was elderly and was appointed general of the rear army.

sentences.zh: 褚淵常詣愿，不在，見其眠牀上積塵埃，有書數袠。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan often called on Yuan; he was not in, and Chu saw dust accumulated on his sleeping couch, with several fascicles of books.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan often visited Yuan; finding him out, he saw dust thick on the sleeping couch and several bundles of books.

sentences.zh: 淵歎曰：「虞君之清，一至於此。

translations.literal: Chu sighed and said, 'Lord Yu's purity reaches even to this.'
translations.idiomatic: Chu sighed and said, 'Lord Yu's integrity extends even to this.'

sentences.zh: 」令人掃地拂牀而去。

translations.literal: ' He had someone sweep the floor and dust the couch, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He had the floor swept and the couch dusted, then left.

sentences.zh: 遷中書郎，領東觀祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Master of Writing in the Secretariat and concurrently Libationer of the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director in the Secretariat and concurrently libationer of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 兄季，爲上虞令，卒。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ji was magistrate of Shangyu and died.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ji, magistrate of Shangyu, died.

sentences.zh: 愿從省步還家，不待詔便歸東。

translations.literal: Yuan walked back home from the Secretariat and, without waiting for an edict, returned east.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan walked home from the Secretariat and, without waiting for imperial permission, returned to the east.

sentences.zh: 除驍騎將軍，遷廷尉，祭酒如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, transferred to Minister of Justice, with the libationer's post as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed general of valiant cavalry, then transferred to minister of justice while retaining his libationer's post.

sentences.zh: 愿嘗事宋明帝，齊初宋神主遷汝陰廟，愿拜辭流涕。

translations.literal: Yuan had once served Emperor Ming of Song. At the beginning of Qi the Song imperial spirit tablets were moved to the Ruyin temple; Yuan bowed in farewell with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had long served Emperor Ming of Song. When the Qi dynasty began and the Song imperial tablets were moved to the temple at Ruyin, he bowed farewell in tears.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jianyuan.

sentences.zh: 年五十四。

translations.literal: He was fifty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 愿著《五經論問》，撰《會稽記》，文翰數十篇。

translations.literal: Yuan authored Discussions and Questions on the Five Classics, compiled Records of Kuaiji, and several tens of literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wrote Discussions and Questions on the Five Classics, compiled Records of Kuaiji, and several dozen essays.

sentences.zh: 劉懷慰字彥泰，平原平原人也。

translations.literal: Liu Huaiwei, style name Yantai, was a man of Pingyuan in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaiwei, courtesy name Yantai, was a native of Pingyuan in Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖奉伯，元嘉中，爲冠軍長史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fengbo, during Yuanjia, was Chief Clerk of the Champion.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fengbo served during the Yuanjia era as chief clerk to the champion general.

sentences.zh: 父乘民，冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chengmin was Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengmin served as inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 懷慰初爲桂陽王征北板行參軍。

translations.literal: Huaiwei at first was Acting Adjutant on the northern campaign staff board of the Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwei began as acting adjutant on the northern campaign staff of the Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 乘民死於義嘉事難，懷慰持喪，不食醯醬，冬月不絮衣。

translations.literal: Chengmin died in the Yijia troubles; Huaiwei observed mourning, ate no pickled sauces, and in winter months wore no padded garments.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmin died in the turmoil of the Yijia era; Huaiwei mourned him without eating pickled foods and wore no padded clothing even in winter.

sentences.zh: 養孤弟妹，事寡叔母，皆有恩義。

translations.literal: He raised orphaned younger siblings and served his widowed aunt by marriage—all with kindness and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his orphaned younger siblings and cared for his widowed aunt by marriage, showing kindness in both.

sentences.zh: 復除邵陵王南中郎參軍，廣德令，尚書駕部郎。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Adjutant of the Southern Gentlemen of the Interior under the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and Master of Writing in the Department of Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed adjutant to the southern gentlemen of the interior under the Prince of Shaoling, magistrate of Guangde, and director in the imperial carriages office of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 懷慰宗從善明等，太祖心腹，懷慰亦豫焉。

translations.literal: Huaiwei's clansmen Shanming and others were the Founder's intimate confidants; Huaiwei also participated therein.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwei's kinsmen Shanming and others were trusted confidants of the Founding Emperor, and Huaiwei was counted among them.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之有舊，令爲書戒喻攸之，太祖省之稱善。

translations.literal: He had old ties with Shen Youzhi and was ordered to write a letter admonishing and instructing Youzhi; the Founder read it and praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: He had old ties with Shen Youzhi and was ordered to write a letter warning him; the Founding Emperor read it and praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was appointed Colonel of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed colonel of foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，上欲置齊郡於京邑，議者以江右土沃，流民所歸，乃治瓜步，以懷慰爲輔國將軍、齊郡太守。

translations.literal: When the State of Qi was established, the sovereign wished to place Qi commandery in the capital region. Discussants said that the lands south of the Yangtze were fertile soil to which floating population returned, so they governed Guabu instead, and Huaiwei was made General Who Supports the State and Grand Administrator of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi state was founded, the emperor wished to establish Qi commandery in the capital region, but advisers argued that the fertile lands south of the Yangtze attracted displaced populations, so the seat was placed at Guabu instead, with Huaiwei appointed general who supports the state and grand administrator of Qi commandery.

sentences.zh: 上謂懷慰曰：「齊邦是王業所基，吾方以爲顯任。

translations.literal: The sovereign said to Huaiwei: "The Qi state is the foundation of our royal enterprise; I intend this as a prominent appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Huaiwei, "The Qi state is the foundation of our royal enterprise, and I intend this as a weighty appointment.

sentences.zh: 經理之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: All matters of administration I entirely entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: All matters of administration I entrust entirely to you.

sentences.zh: 」又手勑曰：「有文事者，必有武備。

translations.literal: " He also wrote a personal edict saying: "Where there are civil affairs, there must also be military preparation.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote a personal edict: "Where there are civil affairs, there must also be military preparedness.

sentences.zh: 今賜卿玉環刀一口。

translations.literal: Now I bestow upon you one jade ring-hilted sword.
translations.idiomatic: I now bestow upon you a jade ring-hilted sword.

sentences.zh: 」懷慰至郡，修治城郭，安集居民，墾廢田二百頃，決沈湖灌溉。

translations.literal: " When Huaiwei reached the commandery, he repaired the walls and moats, settled and gathered the inhabitants, reclaimed two hundred qing of abandoned fields, and opened Shen Lake for irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: " When Huaiwei arrived at the commandery, he repaired the walls and moats, settled the people, reclaimed two hundred qing of abandoned fields, and opened Shen Lake for irrigation.

sentences.zh: 不受禮謁，民有餉其新米一斛者，懷慰出所食麥飯示之，曰：「旦食有餘，幸不煩此。

translations.literal: He accepted no gifts or visits. When a commoner brought him one hu of new rice as tribute, Huaiwei brought out the barley meal he was eating and showed it to him, saying: "My morning meal still has surplus; kindly do not trouble yourself with this.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted no gifts or courtesy calls. When a commoner brought him one hu of new rice, Huaiwei showed him the barley meal he was eating and said, "My morning meal still leaves me with plenty; please do not trouble yourself.

sentences.zh: 」因著《廉吏論》以達其意。

translations.literal: " He therefore wrote An Essay on Incorrupt Officials to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wrote An Essay on Incorrupt Officials to make his meaning clear.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，手勑褒賞。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor heard of it and wrote a personal edict commending and rewarding him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor heard of it and sent a personal edict commending and rewarding him.

sentences.zh: 進督秦、沛二郡。

translations.literal: He was promoted to oversee the two commanderies of Qin and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to oversee the commanderies of Qin and Pei.

sentences.zh: 妻子在都，賜米三百斛。

translations.literal: His wife and children were in the capital; he was granted three hundred hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children remained in the capital, and he was granted three hundred hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 兖州刺史柳世隆與懷慰書曰：「膠東淵化，潁川致美，以今方古，曾何足云。

translations.literal: Yanzhou Inspector Liu Shilong wrote to Huaiwei: "Jiaodong's deep transformation and Yingchuan's bringing of beauty—compared with the present, what are those worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou inspector Liu Shilong wrote to Huaiwei, "Jiaodong's deep transformation and Yingchuan's bringing of beauty—set against your work today, what are those old examples even worth mentioning?

sentences.zh: 」在郡二年，遷正員郎，領青冀二州中正。

translations.literal: " After two years in the commandery, he was transferred to regular staff gentleman and concurrently served as chief arbiter for Qing and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: " After two years in the commandery, he was promoted to regular staff gentleman and concurrently served as chief arbiter for Qing and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 懷慰本名聞慰，世祖卽位，以與舅氏名同，勑改之。

translations.literal: Huaiwei's original name was Wenwei; when Emperor Wu ascended the throne, because it was the same as his maternal uncle's name, an edict changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaiwei's original name was Wenwei; when Emperor Wu took the throne, an edict changed it because it matched his maternal uncle's name.

sentences.zh: 出監東陽郡，爲吏民所安。

translations.literal: He went out as overseer of Dongyang commandery and was trusted by officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as overseer of Dongyang commandery, where officials and commoners alike found security under his rule.

sentences.zh: 還兼安陸王北中郎司馬。

translations.literal: Upon return he also served as Northern Gentlemen of the Interior aide-de-camp to the Prince of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he also served as northern gentlemen of the interior aide-de-camp to the Prince of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Yongming.

sentences.zh: 年四十五。

translations.literal: He was forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，謂僕射徐孝嗣曰：「劉懷慰若在，朝廷不憂無清吏也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he said to Chief Minister Xu Xiaosi: "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would not worry about lacking incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he said to chief minister Xu Xiaosi, "If Liu Huaiwei were still alive, the court would never worry about lacking incorrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 」懷慰與濟陽江淹、陳郡袁彖善，亦著文翰。

translations.literal: " Huaiwei was on good terms with Jiang Yan of Jiyang and Yuan Luan of Chen commandery; he also wrote literary works.
translations.idiomatic: " Huaiwei was on good terms with Jiang Yan of Jiyang and Yuan Luan of Chen commandery, and he also wrote literary works.

sentences.zh: 永明初，獻《皇德論》云。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he presented An Essay on Imperial Virtue, which says:
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongming reign he submitted An Essay on Imperial Virtue, which reads:

sentences.zh: 裴昭明，河東聞喜人，宋太中大夫松之孫也。

translations.literal: Pei Zhaoming was a man of Wenxi in Hedong, grandson of Song Grand Master of Palace Attendants Pei Songzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhaoming was a native of Wenxi in Hedong commandery and a grandson of the Song dynasty grand master of palace attendants Pei Songzhi.

sentences.zh: 父駰，南中郎參軍。

translations.literal: His father Yin was adjutant of the Southern Gentlemen of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin served as adjutant to the southern gentlemen of the interior.

sentences.zh: 昭明少傳儒史之業。

translations.literal: Zhaoming from youth inherited the study of Confucian learning and history.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhaoming inherited the family tradition of Confucian learning and historical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，爲太學博士。

translations.literal: During Taishi he served as Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi reign he served as erudite of the imperial university.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「太子婚，納徵用玉璧虎皮，未詳何所准據。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "For the crown prince's marriage, betrothal gifts use jade discs and tiger skins; it is unclear on what authority this rests.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials memorialized, "For the crown prince's marriage, betrothal gifts include jade discs and tiger skins, but it is unclear what canonical authority this follows.

sentences.zh: 」昭明議：「禮納徵，儷皮爲庭實，鹿皮也。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming argued: "According to the rites for betrothal gifts, paired skins serve as court offerings—these are deer skins.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming argued, "In the rites for betrothal gifts, paired skins serve as court offerings, and those skins are deer hides.

sentences.zh: 晉太子納妃注『以虎皮二』。

translations.literal: The commentary on the Jin crown prince taking a consort states 'using two tiger skins.'
translations.idiomatic: The commentary on the Jin crown prince taking a consort says, 'using two tiger skins.'

sentences.zh: 太元中，公主納徵，虎豹皮各一。

translations.literal: In the Taixuan era, for a princess's betrothal gifts, one each of tiger and leopard skins were used.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taixuan era, when a princess received betrothal gifts, one tiger skin and one leopard skin were used.

sentences.zh: 豈其謂婚禮不詳。

translations.literal: Could this mean that the marriage rites were not clearly specified?
translations.idiomatic: Was this because the marriage rites were not clearly specified?

sentences.zh: 王公之差，故取虎豹文蔚以尊其事。

translations.literal: Because of the difference in rank between princes and dukes, tiger and leopard skins with splendid patterns were taken to honor the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Because princes and dukes differ in rank, tiger and leopard skins with splendid markings were chosen to honor the occasion.

sentences.zh: 虎豹雖文，而徵禮所不言，熊羆雖古，而婚禮所不及，珪璋雖美，或爲用各異。

translations.literal: Tiger and leopard skins, though patterned, are not mentioned in the betrothal rites; bear and brown bear skins, though ancient, are not covered by marriage rites; jade tablets and scepters, though beautiful, may be used differently in each case.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger and leopard skins may be splendid, but the betrothal rites say nothing of them; bear and brown bear skins may be ancient, but marriage rites do not mention them; jade tablets and scepters may be fine, yet their use varies from case to case.

sentences.zh: 今宜准的經誥，凡諸僻謬，一皆詳正。

translations.literal: Now we should take the canonical scriptures as the standard and correct in detail all irregular and erroneous practices.
translations.idiomatic: Now the canonical scriptures should be taken as the standard, and every irregular or mistaken practice should be corrected in detail.

sentences.zh: 」於是有司參議，加珪璋，豹熊羆皮各二。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the responsible officials deliberated together and added jade scepters and two each of leopard, bear, and brown bear skins.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the responsible officials deliberated together and added jade scepters, with two each of leopard, bear, and brown bear skins.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，出爲長沙郡丞，罷任，刺史王蘊謂之曰：「卿清貧，必無還資。

translations.literal: During Yuanhui he went out as assistant administrator of Changsha commandery; when he left office, Inspector Wang Yun said to him: "You are incorrupt and poor—you surely have no returning funds.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhui reign he went out as assistant administrator of Changsha commandery; when he left office, inspector Wang Yun said to him, "You are incorrupt and poor, so you surely have no returning funds.

sentences.zh: 湘中人士有須一禮之命者，我不愛也。

translations.literal: If any gentleman of Xiangzhou needs a nominal appointment, I would not begrudge it.
translations.idiomatic: If any gentleman in Xiangzhou needs a nominal appointment, I would not begrudge giving it.

sentences.zh: 」昭明曰：「下官忝爲邦佐，不能光益上府，豈以鴻都之事仰累清風。

translations.literal: " Zhaoming said: "This humble official, unworthy as a commandery assistant, has been unable to bring luster and benefit to your superior office—how could I burden your upright reputation with such self-serving requests?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming said, "This humble official, though unworthy as a commandery assistant, has been unable to bring luster to your superior office—how could I impose such self-serving requests upon your unsullied reputation?

sentences.zh: 」歷祠部通直郎。

translations.literal: " He successively served as Direct Attendant in the Department of Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: " He later served as direct attendant in the department of sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，使虜，世祖謂之曰：「以卿有將命之才，使還，當以一郡相賞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming he was sent as envoy to the northern barbarians; Emperor Wu said to him: "Because you have talent for bearing imperial orders, when you return I shall reward you with a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming he was sent as envoy to the northern barbarians; Emperor Wu said to him, "Because you have talent for bearing imperial orders, when you return I shall reward you with a commandery.

sentences.zh: 」還爲始安內史。

translations.literal: " Upon return he became interior steward of Shian.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return he was appointed interior steward of Shian.

sentences.zh: 郡民龔玄宣，云神人與其玉印玉板書，不須筆，吹紙便成字。

translations.literal: A district resident, Gong Xuanxuan, claimed that a spirit man gave him a jade seal and jade tablet writing; without a brush, he need only blow on paper and characters would form.
translations.idiomatic: A district resident named Gong Xuanxuan claimed that a spirit had given him a jade seal and jade tablet for writing; without a brush, he need only blow on paper and characters would appear.

sentences.zh: 自稱「龔聖人」，以此惑衆。

translations.literal: He called himself "the Sage Gong" and used this to delude the masses.
translations.idiomatic: He called himself "the Sage Gong" and used this to mislead the people.

sentences.zh: 前後郡守敬事之，昭明付獄治罪。

translations.literal: Previous grand administrators had treated him with reverence; Zhaoming handed him over to prison for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Previous grand administrators had treated him with reverence, but Zhaoming handed him over to prison for punishment.

sentences.zh: 及還，甚貧罄。

translations.literal: When he returned he was utterly destitute.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from office he was utterly destitute.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「裴昭明罷郡還，遂無宅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu said: "Pei Zhaoming returned from leaving a commandery and has no house at all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said, "Pei Zhaoming returned from leaving a commandery and has no house at all.

sentences.zh: 我不諳書，不知古人中誰比？

translations.literal: I am not versed in books—who among the ancients compares with him?
translations.idiomatic: I am not versed in books—who among the ancients compares with him?

sentences.zh: 」遷射聲校尉。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to colonel of the archers who shoot at sound.

sentences.zh: 九年，復遣北使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again sent as envoy to the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was again sent as envoy to the north.

sentences.zh: 建武初，爲王玄邈安北長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he served as Chief Secretary for Pacification of the North under Wang Xuanyao and Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianwu reign he served as chief secretary for pacification of the north under Wang Xuanyao and grand administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 明帝以其在事無所啓奏，代還，責之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, because during his tenure he had submitted no memorials, replaced and recalled him and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, because during his tenure he had submitted no memorials, replaced and recalled him and reproached him.

sentences.zh: 昭明曰：「臣不欲競執關楗故耳。

translations.literal: Zhaoming said: "Your servant did not wish to compete over holding the gate bars, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoming said, "Your servant did not wish to compete over holding the gate bars, that is all.

sentences.zh: 」昭明歷郡皆有勤績，常謂人曰：「人生何事須聚蓄，一身之外，亦復何須？

translations.literal: " Zhaoming in every commandery he served had diligent achievements; he often told people: "What in life requires hoarding? Beyond one's own person, what else is needed?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaoming achieved diligent results in every commandery he served and often told people, "What in life requires hoarding? Beyond one's own person, what else is needed?

sentences.zh: 子孫若不才，我聚彼散；

translations.literal: If descendants lack talent, what I gather they will squander;
translations.idiomatic: If one's descendants lack talent, what one gathers they will squander;

sentences.zh: 若能自立，則不如一經。

translations.literal: If they can stand on their own, one classic is better than wealth.
translations.idiomatic: If they can stand on their own, one classic is worth more than a fortune.

sentences.zh: 」故終身不治產業。

translations.literal: " Therefore throughout his life he did not manage property or estates.
translations.idiomatic: " Therefore he never managed property or estates throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 從祖弟顗，字彥齊。

translations.literal: His younger clansman cousin Yi, courtesy name Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger clansman cousin Yi, courtesy name Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 少有異操。

translations.literal: From youth he had unusual principles.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he held unusual principles.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，於總明觀聽講，不讓劉秉席，秉用爲參軍。

translations.literal: During Taishi, while listening to lectures at Zongming Observatory, he would not yield his seat to Liu Bing; Bing employed him as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi reign, while listening to lectures at Zongming Observatory, he would not yield his seat to Liu Bing, who then employed him as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 昇明末，爲奉朝請。

translations.literal: Late in the Shengming era he served as attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Shengming era he served as attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，世子裴妃須外戚譜，顗不與，遂分籍。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established, the crown prince's Pei consort needed a maternal relatives' genealogy; Yi refused to provide it, and they therefore split the registry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established, the crown prince's Pei consort needed a genealogy of maternal relatives; Yi refused to provide it, and they therefore split the family registry.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，上表誹謗，掛冠去，伏誅。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication, Yi submitted a memorial slandering the court, hung up his cap and departed; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor accepted the abdication, Yi submitted a memorial slandering the court, resigned his office, and fled; he was executed.

sentences.zh: 沈憲字彥璋，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Xian, courtesy name Yanehang, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Xian, courtesy name Yanehang, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖說道，巴西梓潼二郡太守，父璞之，北中郎行參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuodao was Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong; his father Puzhi was acting adjutant of the Northern Gentlemen of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuodao served as grand administrator of Baxi and Zitong commanderies; his father Puzhi served as acting adjutant to the northern gentlemen of the interior.

sentences.zh: 憲初應州辟，爲主簿。

translations.literal: Xian first responded to a provincial summons and served as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xian first answered a provincial summons and served as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 少有幹局，歷臨首、餘杭令，巴陵王府佐，帶襄令，除駕部郎。

translations.literal: From youth he had capacity and foresight; he successively served as magistrate of Linshou and Yuhang, staff officer in the Prince of Baling's household, concurrently magistrate of Xiang, and was appointed director in the imperial carriages office.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed capacity and foresight; he successively served as magistrate of Linshou and Yuhang, staff officer in the Prince of Baling's household, concurrently magistrate of Xiang, and was appointed director in the imperial carriages office.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝與憲棋，謂憲曰：「卿，廣州刺史才也。

translations.literal: Song Emperor Ming played weiqi with Xian and said to him: "You have the makings of a Grand Administrator of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Emperor Ming played weiqi with Xian and said to him, "You have the makings of a grand administrator of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 」補烏程令，甚著政績。

translations.literal: " He was appointed magistrate of Wucheng and achieved notable administrative accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed magistrate of Wucheng and achieved notable administrative results.

sentences.zh: 太守褚淵歎之曰：「此人方員可施。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Chu Yuan sighed and said: "This man can be deployed whether the task is square or round.
translations.idiomatic: Grand administrator Chu Yuan sighed and said, "This man can be deployed whether the task is square or round.

sentences.zh: 」除通直郎，都水使者。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Direct Attendant and Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed direct attendant and commissioner of waterways.

sentences.zh: 長於吏事，居官有績。

translations.literal: He excelled at administrative affairs and in office had achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at administrative affairs and achieved solid results in every post he held.

sentences.zh: 除正員郎，補吳令，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed regular staff gentleman, supplementing as magistrate of Wu, and Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed regular staff gentleman, supplemented as magistrate of Wu, and left assistant director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，西中郎將晃爲豫州，太祖擢憲爲晃長史，南梁太守，行州事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, when General of the Western Gentlemen of the Interior Huang was at Yuzhou, the Founding Emperor promoted Xian to Huang's chief secretary, Grand Administrator of Nanliang, acting in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming, when General of the Western Gentlemen of the Interior Huang was posted to Yuzhou, the Founding Emperor promoted Xian to Huang's chief secretary, grand administrator of Nanliang, and acting provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 遷豫章王諮議，未拜，坐事免官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Advisory Counselor under the Prince of Yuzhang; before assuming the post he was dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to advisory counselor under the Prince of Yuzhang, but before he could assume the post he was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 復除安成王冠軍、武陵王征虜參軍，遷少府卿。

translations.literal: He was again appointed adjutant to the Champion under the Prince of Ancheng and adjutant to the Barbarian Subduer under the Prince of Wuling, then promoted to Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed adjutant to the champion under the Prince of Ancheng and adjutant to the barbarian subduer under the Prince of Wuling, then promoted to director of the palace treasury.

sentences.zh: 少府管掌市易，與民交關，有吏能者，皆更此職。

translations.literal: The Palace Treasury managed market transactions and had dealings with the people; those with administrative talent were usually rotated through this post.
translations.idiomatic: The palace treasury managed market transactions and dealt directly with the people, so officials with real administrative talent were usually rotated through this post.

sentences.zh: 遷王儉鎮軍長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Secretary to the Pacification Army under Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief secretary to the pacification army under Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄爲會稽，以憲爲左軍司馬。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wuling Ye was at Kuaiji, Xian was made Left Army aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wuling Ye was posted to Kuaiji, Xian was made left army aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 太祖以山陰戶衆難治，欲分爲兩縣。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, because Shanyin's population was large and difficult to govern, wished to divide it into two counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor, because Shanyin's population was large and difficult to govern, wished to divide the county in two.

sentences.zh: 世祖啓曰：「縣豈不可治，但用不得其人耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu submitted a memorial saying: "The county is not untamable—only the wrong man has been put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu submitted a memorial saying, "The county is not untamable—it is only that the wrong man has been put in charge.

sentences.zh: 」乃以憲帶山陰令，政聲大著。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xian was appointed concurrently magistrate of Shanyin, and his reputation for good governance became widely noted.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Xian was appointed concurrently magistrate of Shanyin, and his reputation for good governance spread widely.

sentences.zh: 孔稚珪請假東歸，謂人曰：「沈令料事特有天才。

translations.literal: Kong Zhigui took leave to return east and said to people: "Magistrate Shen's handling of affairs shows a special genius for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhigui took leave to return east and said to people, "Magistrate Shen's handling of affairs shows a special genius for judgment.

sentences.zh: 」加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: " He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given the additional title general who pacifies the north.

sentences.zh: 王敬則爲會稽，憲仍留爲鎮軍長史，令如故。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze was at Kuaiji, Xian remained as chief secretary to the Pacification Army, with his magistracy unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze was posted to Kuaiji, Xian remained chief secretary to the pacification army, with his magistracy unchanged.

sentences.zh: 遷爲冠軍長史，行南豫州事，晉安王後軍長史、廣陵太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief secretary under the Champion, acting in Southern Yuzhou affairs, then chief secretary to the Rear Army under the Prince of Jin'an and Grand Administrator of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief secretary under the champion and acting governor of Southern Yuzhou, then chief secretary to the rear army under the Prince of Jin'an and grand administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 西陽王子明代爲南兖州，憲仍留爲冠軍長史，太守如故，頻行州府事。

translations.literal: When Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, was at Southern Yanzhou, Xian remained chief secretary under the Champion with his grand administrator post unchanged, repeatedly acting in provincial and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, was posted to Southern Yanzhou, Xian remained chief secretary under the champion with his grand administrator post unchanged, repeatedly acting in provincial and prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 永明八年，子明典籤劉道濟取府州五十人役自給，又役子明左右，及船仗贓私百萬，爲有司所奏，世祖怒，賜道濟死。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's chief clerk Liu Daoji conscripted fifty men from the prefecture and province for his own use, also used labor from Ziming's personal attendants, and embezzled a million in ships, arms, and private goods; memorialized by the responsible officials, Emperor Wu was furious and ordered Daoji to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming, Ziming's chief clerk Liu Daoji conscripted fifty men from the prefecture and province for his own use, also used labor from Ziming's personal attendants, and embezzled a million in ships, arms, and private goods; when the responsible officials memorialized the case, Emperor Wu was furious and ordered Daoji to death.

sentences.zh: 憲坐不糾，免官。

translations.literal: Xian was punished for failing to investigate and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was punished for failing to investigate and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋復爲長史、輔國將軍，以疾去官。

translations.literal: Soon after he was again appointed chief secretary and General Who Supports the State, then left office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was again appointed chief secretary and general who supports the state, then left office due to illness.

sentences.zh: 除散騎常侍，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: He was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary but died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary but died before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 當世稱爲良吏。

translations.literal: His contemporaries acclaimed him as a good official.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries acclaimed him as a good official.

sentences.zh: 憲同郡丘仲起，先是爲晉平郡，清廉自立。

translations.literal: Xian's fellow townsman Qiu Zhongqi had earlier served as magistrate of Jinping and maintained himself in integrity and self-restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's fellow townsman Qiu Zhongqi had earlier served as magistrate of Jinping and maintained himself in integrity and self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 褚淵歎曰：「見可欲心能不亂，此楊公所以遺子孫也。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan sighed and said: "The heart that can remain unperturbed when seeing what is desirable—this is what Duke Yang bequeathed to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan sighed and said, "The heart that can remain unperturbed when seeing what is desirable—this is what Duke Yang bequeathed to his descendants.

sentences.zh: 」仲起字子震，少爲憲從伯領軍寅之所知。

translations.literal: " Zhongqi, courtesy name Zizhen, from youth was recognized by Xian's elder clansman uncle, Army Control Officer Yin.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongqi, courtesy name Zizhen, from youth was recognized by Xian's elder clansman uncle, army control officer Yin.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽中，爲太子領軍長史，官至廷尉。

translations.literal: During Song Yuanhui he served as chief secretary to the Army Control Officer of the Crown Prince and rose to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song dynasty's Yuanhui reign he served as chief secretary to the crown prince's army control officer and rose to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 李珪之字孔璋，江夏鍾武人也。

translations.literal: Li Guizhi, courtesy name Kongzhang, was a man of Zhongwu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guizhi, courtesy name Kongzhang, was a native of Zhongwu in Jiangxia commandery.

sentences.zh: 父祖皆爲縣令。

translations.literal: His father and grandfather had both been county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: His father and grandfather had both served as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 珪之少辟州從事。

translations.literal: Guizhi in youth was summoned as provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Guizhi was summoned as provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，蔡興宗爲郢州，以珪之爲安西府佐，委以職事，清治見知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song Taishi, when Cai Xingzong was at Yingzhou, he made Guizhi a staff officer in the Pacification of the West headquarters, entrusted him with official duties, and was known for his clean administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty's Taishi reign, when Cai Xingzong was posted to Yingzhou, he made Guizhi a staff officer in the pacification of the west headquarters, entrusted him with official duties, and came to be known for his clean administration.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮西中郎諮議，右軍將軍，兼都水使者。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Advisory Counselor under the Western Gentlemen of the Interior, General of the Right Army, and concurrently Commissioner of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to advisory counselor under the western gentlemen of the interior, general of the right army, and concurrently commissioner of waterways.

sentences.zh: 珪之歷職稱爲清能，除游擊將軍，兼使者如故。

translations.literal: In every post Guizhi was praised as pure and capable; he was appointed General Who Suppresses Insurgents, with the concurrent envoy post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In every office he held, Guizhi was praised for integrity and competence; he was appointed general who suppresses insurgents while retaining his concurrent envoy post.

sentences.zh: 轉兼少府，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to concurrent Minister of the Palace Supplies and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to concurrent minister of the palace supplies and died.

sentences.zh: 先是，四年，滎陽毛惠素爲少府卿，吏才強而治事清刻。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fourth year, Mao Huisu of Xingyang was Minister of the Palace Supplies—a man of strong administrative talent who governed affairs with austere clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the fourth year, Mao Huisu of Xingyang served as minister of the palace supplies; he was a forceful administrator who ran affairs with austere precision.

sentences.zh: 勑市銅官碧青一千二百斤供御畫，用錢六十萬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the purchase from the copper office of twelve hundred jin of malachite blue-green for imperial painting, at a cost of six hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the purchase of twelve hundred jin of malachite pigment from the copper office for imperial painting, at a cost of six hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 有讒惠素納利者，世祖怒，勑尚書評賈，貴二十八萬餘，有司奏之，伏誅。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Huisu for taking profit. Emperor Wu grew angry and ordered the Masters of Writing to assess the price; it was valued at a little over two hundred eighty thousand, the relevant offices memorialized, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Huisu of taking a kickback. Emperor Wu was furious and ordered the Masters of Writing to reassess the price at just over two hundred eighty thousand cash; the authorities memorialized the case, and Huisu was executed.

sentences.zh: 死後家徒四壁，上甚悔恨。

translations.literal: After his death his house held only bare walls; the sovereign deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his home was utterly bare, and the emperor deeply regretted what had been done.

sentences.zh: 孔琇之，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Kong Xiuzhi was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xiuzhi was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖季恭，光祿大夫，父靈運，著作郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jigong was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; his father Lingyun was Master of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jigong served as grand master of splendid happiness; his father Lingyun served as master of composition.

sentences.zh: 琇之初爲國子生，舉孝廉。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi at first was a student of the Imperial Academy and was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi first entered the Imperial Academy and was recommended as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 除衞軍行參軍，員外郎，尚書三公郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Guard Army, Outside-Office Gentleman, and Master of Writing in the Department of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting adjutant of the guard army, outside-office gentleman, and director in the three dukes office of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 出爲烏程令，有吏能。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Wucheng and had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as magistrate of Wucheng, where he proved a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 還遷通直郎，補吳令。

translations.literal: On return he was transferred to Regular Emergent Attendant and appointed magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was promoted to regular emergent attendant and appointed magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 有小兒年十歲，偷刈隣家稻一束，琇之付獄治罪，或諫之，琇之曰：「十歲便能爲盜，長大何所不爲？

translations.literal: There was a small boy ten years old who stole and reaped one sheaf of his neighbor's rice. Xiuzhi sent him to prison to be punished. Some admonished him; Xiuzhi said, 'At ten he can already be a thief—when grown, what will he not do?'
translations.idiomatic: A ten-year-old boy stole and reaped one sheaf of a neighbor's rice. Xiuzhi had him thrown in prison. When some tried to dissuade him, he said, 'If he can steal at ten, what will he not do when he grows up?'

sentences.zh: 」縣中皆震肅。

translations.literal: ' Throughout the district all were awed into reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The whole district was awed into strict order.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，又以職事知名。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing and again became known for his official duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left assistant director in the Masters of Writing and again won renown for his competence in office.

sentences.zh: 轉前軍將軍，兼少府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Forward Army and concurrently Minister of the Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general of the forward army and concurrently minister of the palace supplies.

sentences.zh: 遷驍騎將軍，少府如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry, with the Ministry of Palace Supplies as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of valiant cavalry while retaining his post at the ministry of palace supplies.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、高宗冠軍征虜長史、江夏內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North, Chief Clerk to the Champion Who Conquers the Barbarians under the High Ancestor, and Interior Minister of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as general who pacifies the north, chief clerk to the champion who conquers the barbarians under the High Ancestor, and interior minister of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 還爲正員常侍，兼左民尚書、廷尉卿。

translations.literal: On return he became Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Master of Writing for the Left People and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed regular attendant-in-ordinary and concurrently director for the left people in the Masters of Writing and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 出爲臨海太守，在任清約，罷郡還，獻乾薑二十斤，世祖嫌少，及知琇之清，乃歎息。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand Administrator of Linhai; in office he was pure and abstemious. When he finished his commandery and returned, he presented twenty jin of dried ginger. Emperor Wu thought it too little, but when he learned of Xiuzhi's purity he sighed.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as grand administrator of Linhai and governed with austere integrity. When his term ended he presented twenty jin of dried ginger as a gift. Emperor Wu at first thought the offering too meager, but on learning how incorrupt Xiuzhi was, he sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 除武陵王前軍長史，未拜，仍出爲輔國將軍，監吳興郡，尋拜太守，治稱清嚴。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Forward Army under the Prince of Wuling but did not receive the appointment; he was still sent out as General Who Supports the State, overseer of Wuxing commandery, and soon appointed Grand Administrator, with governance praised as pure and stern.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk to the forward army of the Prince of Wuling but never took up the post; instead he was sent out as general who supports the state to oversee Wuxing commandery, soon confirmed as grand administrator, where his rule was praised as pure and stern.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：琴瑟不調，必解而更張也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When lute and zither are out of tune, one must loosen and restring them.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: When the lute and zither are out of tune, the strings must be loosened and restrung.

sentences.zh: 魏晉爲吏，稍與漢乖，苛猛之風雖衰，而仁愛之情亦減。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin, serving as officials gradually diverged from Han ways; though the wind of harsh severity declined, the feeling of benevolent love also diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin, official service gradually diverged from Han practice; though harsh severity faded, benevolent concern diminished as well.

sentences.zh: 局以峻法，限以常條，以必世之仁未及宣理，而朞月之望已求治術。

translations.literal: Confined by severe laws and bounded by routine statutes, the benevolence that must last generations had not yet reached full expression in governance, yet the hope of a single month already demanded techniques of order.
translations.idiomatic: Bound by harsh statutes and routine regulations, the enduring benevolence needed for true governance had scarcely begun to take effect before a single month's tenure already demanded visible results.

sentences.zh: 先公後私，在己未易，割民奉國，於物非難，期之救過，所利苟免。

translations.literal: Putting the public first and the private second was not easy for oneself; cutting the people to serve the state was not hard in outward terms—what was sought was rescue from faults, the benefit sought was mere escape.
translations.idiomatic: Putting public duty before private interest was hard to sustain in oneself, while extracting from the people to serve the state was all too easy in practice; officials aimed only to cover their mistakes and secure their own escape from blame.

sentences.zh: 且目見可欲，嗜好方流，貪以敗官，取與違義，吏之不臧，罔非由此。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the eye sees what is desirable, appetites then flow forth; greed ruins office, taking and giving violate righteousness—there is no corruption of officials that does not arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when the eye sees what it desires, appetite follows; greed ruins office, and wrongful taking and giving violate duty—there is scarcely any official corruption that does not spring from this.

sentences.zh: 擿姦辯偽，誠俟異識，垂名著績，唯有廉平。

translations.literal: Exposing treachery and distinguishing falsehood truly await unusual insight; to leave a famous name and recorded achievement—only integrity and fairness will do.
translations.idiomatic: Exposing fraud and distinguishing falsehood truly requires exceptional insight; to leave a lasting name and recorded achievement, nothing suffices but integrity and fairness.

sentences.zh: 今世之治民，未有出於此也。

translations.literal: In governing the people in the present age, nothing has gone beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: In governing the people today, nothing goes beyond this principle.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：蒸蒸小民，吏職長親。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The common people thrive and grow; the official's duty is to be their elder and kin.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: The common people flourish and multiply; the official's duty is to be their elder and kin.

sentences.zh: 棼亂須理，卹隱歸仁。

translations.literal: When tangled disorder must be set right, comfort the hidden and return to benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: When disorder must be untangled, comfort the suffering and return to benevolence.

sentences.zh: 枉直交瞀，寬猛代陳。

translations.literal: Crooked and straight cross in confusion; lenience and severity succeed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong cross in confusion; lenience and severity alternate in turn.

sentences.zh: 伊何導物，貴在清身。

translations.literal: By what means to guide all things? What is prized is a pure person.
translations.idiomatic: By what means shall one guide the people? What matters most is integrity in one's own person.

translations.literal: Footnote one.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial note marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses as the collated edition the *Book of Southern Qi*, January 1972 edition, Zhonghua Book Company.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the January 1972 Zhonghua Book Company edition of the *Book of Southern Qi*.
